correctness.rationale: Starting with c_n=A_n/n!, the positive recurrence is majorized by H=z+2H², giving radius R≥1/8, and G=G²+2G(z/2). For real 0<z<R the derivative identity gives G<1/2 and z≤G−G²≤1/4. At the finite positive radius R, Pringsheim and the implicit function theorem force G(R−)=1/2: otherwise the implicit derivative 1−2G would not vanish there. The holomorphic half-argument is still inside its convergence disk, and G(R/2)=1/8. Evaluating at consecutive half-arguments yields the stated orbit; the derivative at zero gives lim 2^j a_j=R. Iteration of (1−2G(z))G'(z)=G'(z/2) gives G'(R/2)=1/P. The orbit decreases at least geometrically and the tails of the two products are bounded below by 1 minus the corresponding sum, giving the published brackets and P>0. For z on |z|=R other than R, the arguments of the n=1 and n=2 terms cannot agree, so |G(z/2)|<G(R/2); the discriminant has no competing zeros. Its simple zero at R has linear term (4R/P)(1−z/R). The square-root branch continues to a dented disk, yielding coefficient amplitude sqrt(R/P)/(2 sqrt(pi)) by square-root transfer. Thus the rate R^(-1) refers to A_n/n!; the moments themselves include n!. The displayed digits and stated width bounds were independently certified with rational Machin bounds for pi, dyadic-grid orbit bounds and rational integer-square-root brackets (python3 /workspace/branches/audit_constants.py; widths about 5.4082e−47 and 5.0032e−47). The frozen verifier was read but not executed; its decimal display is not the basis for the rational certification. This is a formal moment-series result, not a proof of a pointwise density tail or of stationary-law existence.
